column1: # The authoritative patch set. Single source of truth.
# apply-patches.py applies these to a staged rootfs when building an image, and
# verify-panel.sh checks the same table against the running panel. Anything that
# needs to know what is patched reads THIS file, so the two cannot drift.
# That drift is not hypothetical: TUXEDO-FIX-STATUS.md spent a release claiming
# /Config and the 6800 listener were outstanding after both had shipped, because
# nothing mechanical contradicted the prose.
# OFFSETS ARE FILE OFFSETS, NOT VIRTUAL ADDRESSES. For Barracuda the two differ
# by 0x8000 (VA 0x3b3b4 is file 0x333b4). Using a VA reads the wrong four bytes.
# COMPLETE as of 2026-09-08, and this was EXECUTED, not asserted. A copy of the
# genuine stock tree at /work/extracted/root_stock was patched with every row:
# "20 sites: 0 already patched, 20 applied, 0 needing attention", and the three
# results matched byte-exactly. Re-run it any time; see below.
#   supervis   04386af2971fc29b63bd6f7a87f2b9e2 -> 6caac69eb46fb78447bcd3032078fa44
# The Barracuda target moved 2026-09-08: it was c8971027 (v12, 11 rows), then
# 55448f05 once the two P13 push-auth rows landed, and is now 3463efcc with the
# seven P14 rows. 3463efcc is what the panel runs.
# ⚠ THE P14 ROWS WERE ADDED AFTER THE FACT AND THAT IS THE HAZARD THIS FILE
# EXISTS TO PREVENT. The thread-leak fix was applied straight to the live panel
# over SSH on 2026-09-08 and was absent here for about an hour. In that window a
# rebuild would have silently reverted it -- an image build stages a fresh tree
# and applies THIS table -- and `verify-panel.sh` reported "panel matches
# expectations, rc=0", because it iterates the rows and an offset absent from
# the table is never read. The panel was ahead of the table and the one
# mechanical check that should have caught it was structurally unable to.
# Anything applied to the panel by hand belongs here in the same action.
# Re-run it on the build VM (stock tree at /work/extracted/root_stock):
#   python3 apply-patches.py --apply --root <copy-of-stock-tree> --table patches.tsv
#   md5sum <tree>/opt/webserver/Barracuda <tree>/tuxedo <tree>/supervis
# It was NOT complete before. The three P1a/P1b/P1c rows below were written by
# hand years before this table existed and were unrecorded, so the 4-byte P1/P2
# rows described only the branch INTO the lockout stub, not the stub itself:
# 119 bytes across 16 runs were missing:
#   VA 0x13a68, 0x13a7c   two bl sites NOP'd to 00 00 a0 e1   (8 bytes)
#   VA 0x15074-0x150ef    resetLoginFailureCount replaced by a hand-written
#                         lockout stub                        (~124 bytes)
# Those belong to P1/P2 and were written by hand before this table existed, so
# the 4-byte rows for P1 and P2 record only the branch INTO the stub, not the
# stub itself.
# Until they were recorded, build-image.sh reproduced v12 only because it starts
# from the v11 payload that already contained them; it could not have rebuilt v12
# from stock. It can now.
# name<TAB>binary<TAB>file_offset<TAB>stock<TAB>patched<TAB>description
